content:
# Sirach 27 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** Sirach 27 | **Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Total Disagreements:** 14

---

## Disagreement 001 — 27:1 "small gain / trifling gain"
**Verse:** 27:1
**EMET:** "for-the-sake-of a-small-gain"
**LOGOS:** "for the sake of a trifling gain"
**PNEUMA:** "chasing a small profit"
**Issue:** βραχέος — "small/little." "Trifling" (LOGOS) adds a dismissive connotation; "small" is more neutral. Both capture the irony (sinning for so little). SOPHIA uses "trifling gain" to sharpen the irony.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "for the sake of trifling gain."

---

## Disagreement 002 — 27:2 "wedge between buying-and-selling / sin between commerce"
**Verse:** 27:2
**EMET:** "so between-buying-and-selling sin will-wedge-itself"
**LOGOS:** "so sin will wedge itself between buying and selling"
**PNEUMA:** "Sin drives itself like a wedge between buyer and seller"
**Issue:** ἀνὰ μέσον ἀγορασμοῦ καὶ πράσεως — "between buying and selling." PNEUMA changes to "buyer and seller" (people, not activities). The Greek refers to the commercial activities, not the persons. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "so sin will wedge itself between buying and selling."

---

## Disagreement 003 — 27:4 "anxious-thought / reflection / reasoning something through"
**Verse:** 27:4
**EMET:** "in-the-anxious-thought of a-man"
**LOGOS:** "in a man's reflection"
**PNEUMA:** "when a person reasons something through"
**Issue:** ἐν διαλογισμῷ ἀνθρώπου — "in the reflection/reasoning of a man." EMET adds "anxious" which is not in the Greek. LOGOS's "reflection" and PNEUMA's "reasoning" are both defensible. SOPHIA uses "in a man's reflection."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "so a man's faults remain in his reflection."

---

## Disagreement 004 — 27:5 furnace metaphor direction
**Verse:** 27:5
**EMET:** "The-furnace tests the-work of-the-potter"
**LOGOS:** "The furnace tests the work of the potter"
**PNEUMA:** "Fire tests what the potter makes; reasoning tests what a person is made of"
**Issue:** κάμινος δοκιμάζει σκεύη χαλκέως — "the furnace tests the vessels of the craftsman/smith." "Potter" vs "smith" — χαλκέως is actually "bronzesmith/craftsman," not "potter." EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA all use "potter" which is a mistranslation. SOPHIA should note: the Greek has "smith/craftsman."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "The furnace tests the work of the craftsman" — correcting the error.

---

## Disagreement 005 — 27:7 "this is the testing of persons"
**Verse:** 27:7
**EMET:** "for this is-the-testing-of-persons"
**LOGOS:** "for this is the testing of persons"
**PNEUMA:** "the proof of a person is in their character"
**Issue:** αὕτη δοκιμασία ἀνθρώπων — "this is the testing/proving of persons." PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the point: the act of hearing/listening before praising IS the test. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "for this is the testing of persons."

---

## Disagreement 006 — 27:9 "birds-of-a-kind / birds of a kind"
**Verse:** 27:9
**EMET:** "Birds-of-a-kind come-to-rest with-their-kind"
**LOGOS:** "Birds of a kind settle among their own kind"
**PNEUMA:** "Birds flock together with their own kind"
**Issue:** ὄρνεα πρὸς τὰ ὅμοια αὐτῶν — "birds toward their like." All capture the meaning. The Greek doesn't say "flock" specifically. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Birds of a kind settle among their own kind."

---

## Disagreement 007 — 27:11 "changes like the moon / shifts around like the phases of the moon"
**Verse:** 27:11
**EMET:** "a-foolish-man changes like the-moon"
**LOGOS:** "a foolish man changes like the moon"
**PNEUMA:** "a fool shifts around like the phases of the moon"
**Issue:** μωρὸς ὡς σελήνη ἀλλοιοῦται — "a fool changes like the moon." PNEUMA's "phases" is accurate but interpretive. The simple image is sufficient. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a foolish man changes like the moon."

---

## Disagreement 008 — 27:13 "licentiousness of sin / wallows in licentiousness"
**Verse:** 27:13
**EMET:** "their-laughter is in-the-licentiousness of-sin"
**LOGOS:** "their laughter wallows in the licentiousness of sin"
**PNEUMA:** "their laughter reeks of sin"
**Issue:** ἐν ἀσελγείαις ἁμαρτίας — "in the licentiousness/wantonness of sin." LOGOS adds "wallows" (interpretive but apt). PNEUMA loses "licentiousness" entirely. SOPHIA uses LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "their laughter wallows in licentiousness."

---

## Disagreement 009 — 27:16 "reveals secrets / betrays secrets / betrays a confidence"
**Verse:** 27:16
**EMET:** "Whoever-reveals secrets"
**LOGOS:** "Whoever betrays secrets"
**PNEUMA:** "Whoever betrays a confidence"
**Issue:** ἀποκαλύπτων μυστήρια — "revealing/uncovering secrets/mysteries." "Betrays" (LOGOS) captures the relational violation better than "reveals." "Confidence" (PNEUMA) for μυστήρια is slightly loose but natural. SOPHIA uses "betrays secrets."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Whoever betrays secrets."

---

## Disagreement 010 — 27:20 "soul is-wounded / wound to his soul" and healing
**Verse:** 27:20
**EMET:** "his-soul is-wounded. There-is-no-more healing — for he-has-been-reviled and insulted"
**LOGOS:** "his soul is wounded; there is no longer any healing, for he has been insulted and reviled"
**PNEUMA:** "The wound to his soul is deep; there's no healing now, after the insults and betrayal"
**Issue:** PNEUMA adds "deep" (not in Greek) and substitutes "betrayal" for "reviled" (ὠνειδίσθη — "was reproached/insulted"). SOPHIA follows LOGOS for accuracy.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "For his soul is wounded; there is no longer any healing, for he has been reviled and insulted."

---

## Disagreement 011 — 27:21 silver and gold recovery metaphor
**Verse:** 27:21
**EMET:** "As-for silver and gold, a-disclosure will-establish them; but as-for you, you-have-been-found-out for your-neighbor's-words"
**LOGOS:** "As for silver and gold, a slip may yet restore them; but as for you, you have been found out for the sake of your neighbor's words"
**PNEUMA:** "Silver and gold can recover from a stumble; but once you're exposed for betraying a friend's words, you can't undo it"
**Issue:** The verse is cryptic. The Greek has ἐπὶ λόγοις τοῦ πλησίον σου — "at the words of your neighbor." The image seems to be: silver and gold can be melted and restored even after a mistake, but you (who betrayed) cannot be restored. LOGOS's "a slip may yet restore them" is interpretive. SOPHIA notes the difficulty.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "As silver and gold may be tested by a slip and recover, so you have been exposed by the words of your neighbor."

---

## Disagreement 012 — 27:25 "stone straight-up" boomerang proverb
**Verse:** 27:25
**EMET:** "Whoever-throws a-stone straight-up — upon his-own-head it-falls"
**LOGOS:** "Whoever throws a stone straight up — it falls upon his own head"
**PNEUMA:** "Throw a stone straight up in the air — it comes back down on your head"
**Issue:** All agents agree on the image. Minor syntactic differences. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Whoever throws a stone straight up — it falls upon his own head."

---

## Disagreement 013 — 27:27 "it-will-roll-back / roll back / come rolling back"
**Verse:** 27:27
**EMET:** "upon him it-will-roll-back"
**LOGOS:** "it will roll back upon him"
**PNEUMA:** "it will come rolling back"
**Issue:** ἀνακυλισθήσεται — "will be rolled back." LOGOS preserves the direction "upon him." PNEUMA loses "upon him." SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "it will roll back upon him."

---

## Disagreement 014 — 27:29 "devout / good people" and "pain will consume"
**Verse:** 27:29
**EMET:** "Those-who-rejoice in-the-fall of-the-devout will-be-caught in a-trap"
**LOGOS:** "Those who rejoice in the downfall of the devout will be caught in a trap"
**PNEUMA:** "Those who gloat over good people's suffering will themselves be trapped"
**Issue:** εὐσεβῶν — "of the devout/pious." "Good people" (PNEUMA) loses the specifically religious term. "Devout" is the correct translation of εὐσεβής. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Those who rejoice in the downfall of the devout will be caught in a trap."
